'dbbib / faed deep analysis' written in a 'certified' style: Bifid key = dbbib first-appearance order; a claimed unique prime-channel parse; a square-confinement argument; a RAW_PW 69-char chain that decrypts the small blob (salt 3ab585348552415d) to 79 bytes and then a second 79-byte layer with salt b45a5e3d827593ca; and an open 'gate' E_S=740a25de4b8e946d0a5ae2667a23a2.

As 8-bit ASCII it holds a reversed line ('HOW_DID_CAESAR_SEND_HIS_MESSAGES?AND_WHAT_IF_13_IS_DEFAULT_AND_THE_NUMBER_C_IS_THE_2ND_HINT?'), Caesar-3 text, and an inner bit-reversed binary that reads 'BASE64' + base64 of a YouTube rickroll URL. Python script, read as text only. It reads hex lines from 'lokerdar.txt', pads each to 256 bits (4 pad/reverse variants), and lays them on a 16x16 bit grid. Transforms: 4 rotations x 4 mirrors x 3 boustrophedon orders, plus each variant XORed with all-ones. Writes hex candidates to 'nosin.txt'. A candidate-key generator; the input list is not included.

LLM-style JS snippet ('Let me analyze the complete puzzle structure...'). It lists the SalPhaseIon a-i stream, the hint 'your first hint is your last command', the two base64 halves of the small blob, 'shabefanstoo' (labelled 'potential password'), and the Cosmic Duality blob. Only console.log output, no new derivation.

leads.claim: RAW_PW = matrixsumlist + enter + lastwordsbeforearchichoice + thispassword + matrixsumlist (69 chars) decrypts the small blob (EVP-MD5, AES-256-CBC, salt 3ab585348552415d) to 79 bytes 'B1_79B.bin' = K_C1||K_C2||E_C. WIF(K_C1) is then the password for a 'p32 outer' layer (salt b45a5e3d827593ca) giving 'B2_79B.bin' = K_S1||K_S2||E_S. Claimed shas 1449a217... / b40fce72...
leads.method: openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -md md5 style EVP_BytesToKey on the 96-byte small blob; parse the plaintext as 32+32+15 bytes
leads.self_verifying: Weak. A 79-byte plaintext means the pad byte was 0x01, which happens for about 1 in 256 wrong keys. Real confirmation needs K_C1/K_C2/K_S* to produce 1GSMG1JC9wtdSwfwApgj2xcmJPAwx7prBe (HASH160 a9553269...) or readable text. The file shows neither, and it does not say where a blob with salt b45a5e3d827593ca exists.

leads.claim: The open 'gate' is a short phrase X with sha256(X).hexdigest()[:30] == E_S (or md5), where E_S = 740a25de4b8e946d0a5ae2667a23a2 (120 bits) is taken from the B2_79B layer. The author says >8.3M window checks and 216 page-group preimages were negative.
leads.self_verifying: A 120-bit prefix match would be unambiguous. But E_S is only meaningful if the RAW_PW chain above is real, and that is unproven (a padding-oracle false positive is likely), so a negative proves nothing.

leads.claim: The 7-token XOR key a795de11... decrypts the 1344-byte Cosmic Duality envelope (AES-256-CBC, MD5 KDF) to 1327 bytes, sha256 4f7a1e4e...c081. A 103x103 matrix derivation (row[i] + col[(i+7) mod 103], base-38 digits ord(c)-80, 68 bytes) gives 'Half', 'Better Half' and trailer fc0c1b02. The author grades this C: reproducible but NOT authenticated.
leads.method: XOR of 7 SalPhaseIon tokens -> AES key; matrix row/col base-38 derivation
leads.self_verifying: Not self-verifying. Valid padding is 1/256 and the 1327 bytes are near-random with no file signature. The author lists exhaustive EC combinations of Half/Better Half against the prize pubkey, all negative.

leads.claim: DBBI-keyed Bifid: keyword dbifhcega, square dbifhcegaklmnopqrstuvwxyz, full-period decode of the 570 FAED symbols gives 'btcseed' + 563 letters (sha256 15d62c82...0507), with exactly one z at position 98. After the 7-char header there are 281+281 rails: a control rail b/c/d/e (b=53, c=89, d=71, e=68) and a carrier rail over 24 letters.
leads.self_verifying: The 'btcseed' header is a 7-letter crib. The 563-letter body is not readable.

leads.claim: In B91 (dbbi) the first five 'b' positions are exactly the primes 2,3,5,7,11 (permutation p=0.00005, pre-registered). Removing all 'g' extends the match to the first nine primes. Pomyk's row-shift claim and J's 'be' separators do not reproduce.
leads.method: position test against primes with a shuffle null
leads.self_verifying: Only a statistic; no decode follows from it.

leads.claim: Of the 2^10 merge-subsets of the 10 'be' pairs in dbbib_91, exactly one parse gives 83 tokens whose 23 prime-position tokens read 11110111001111011001100 (= phase-1 seed 0xF73D92 with the last bit dropped and a 1 inserted at bit 21). The 60-char payload then splits 19|16|23 at 'b' separators.
leads.method: be-pair merge enumeration + prime positions as bits
leads.self_verifying: No. The 'match' needs an ad-hoc edit (drop a bit, insert a 1), so it is post-hoc.

leads.claim: Square-confinement argument: in any keyword-keyed 5x5 square the 9 key letters sit in rows 0-1, so a keyword Bifid row-stream of dbbib/faed is binary. Only a hand-placed 'interpreter alphabet' square could work. Byte ceilings: 91 tokens -> <=38 bytes, 570 -> <=237 bytes; a 29M-form injective digit-map sweep found nothing >=80% printable.
leads.self_verifying: A negative and structural result. It matches cycle-37 closures 2 and 5.

leads.claim: Known solved layers re-derived: Phase-1 counter-clockwise spiral -> gsmg.io/theseedisplanted (blue=1, yellow=0, coloured cells = last bit of each of the 24 chars, #fefefe at spiral pos 163); Phase 3.2 Beaufort key thematrixhasyou over a 26-symbol alphabet; VIC checkerboard (prefixes 1 and 4) -> INCASEYOUMANAGE...NEEDFUNDSTOLIVE; z-segments -> lastwordsbeforearchichoice / thispassword.
leads.method: spiral read, Beaufort, straddling checkerboard, letters->decimal->hex

leads.claim: The Architect text phrase 'over twenty-three ciphers, sixteen encryptions and/or seven intertwined passwords' encodes 23 XOR 16 = 7, meaning XOR is the maker's combining operation. Also, '1812' = R(18) A(1) B(2) = 'RAB' (rabbits nest), not a bit length; the contiguous a-i run is 765 = 91+104+570 symbols (2295 bits).
leads.self_verifying: No. Interpretive, with no direct operational test.

leads.claim: Corrections: issue #69 key 818af53d... gives no valid PKCS#7 padding on the Cosmic envelope; 'Dualite', 'yourlastcommand' and 'secondanswer' do not appear in the raw page HTML (page 4533 bytes, no comments/scripts); 17ucy1K9ZUAaoY6JVtM932W9jUp5LXfyHa (3.75 BTC) is a self-transfer, not a target. leads.method: page byte check, padding check, chain inspection
leads.self_verifying: Yes for the padding and markup claims. The 17ucy role is inference (the dbbib file instead calls it a funded 'dualite' escrow gate).

leads.claim: Procedure: treat each 256-bit candidate (hex) as a 16x16 bit grid and emit 4 pad variants x 4 rotations x 4 mirrors x 3 row orders (plain/boustrophedon), each also XOR all-ones, as private-key candidates. The input list 'lokerdar.txt' is not provided. The turn2left helper is dead code.
leads.self_verifying: Would self-verify by address match if the inputs were known. They are not, and grid transforms of known 256-bit values are a small family.

leads.claim: The 5368-bit string decodes (8-bit ASCII) to: reversed 'HOW_DID_CAESAR_SEND_HIS_MESSAGES?AND_WHAT_IF_13_IS_DEFAULT_AND_THE_NUMBER_C_IS_THE_2ND_HINT?'; Caesar-3 'uhpryhwkhfruuhfwklqwwrsurfhhgwrwkhqhawvwdjh' = 'remove the correct hint to proceed to the next stage'; an inner ASCII-0/1 run which, bit-reversed, reads 'BASE64aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1kUXc0dzlXZ1hjUQ==' (a rickroll URL, not visited); trailer 'hvuhyhu' = Caesar-3 of 'esrever'.
leads.self_verifying: Yes: it decodes to readable text and resolves to a troll payload. No GSMG value.

leads.claim: Unrelated CTF technique: EXIF tags hold 0/1/space strings of length 1681 = 41x41. Mask the 'Wh 173 R4b B17' string with the module matrix of a regenerated QR ('This is the key. Now... follow the white rabbit.'), keep the bits at dark modules, and read them as binary ASCII.
exact_strings: This is the key. Now... follow the white rabbit.
leads.self_verifying: Not about GSMG. Cycle 37 already found no hidden channels in the GSMG images.
